verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off'; R2: 'blasted off ... on Wednesday' (April 1, 2026); R3: 'At 6:35 p.m. ET ... lifting off'; R4: 'lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm successful launch on April 1, 2026 with post-liftoff updates.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time'; R3: 'At 6:35 p.m. ET'; R4: 'lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state the exact launch time as 6:35 p.m. EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center'; R4: 'Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly specify Kennedy Space Center, Florida as launch site.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket carried four astronauts in the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket ... Orion crew capsule'; R2: 'NASA rocket ... Orion capsule ... four astronauts'; R3: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket ... Orion spacecraft and its crew of four'; R4: 'Space Launch System rocket ... Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS launched Orion with four astronauts aboard.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission to fly around the Moon and return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day moon mission ... loop around it ... splashdown on April 10'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: '10-day mission around the moon'; R4: '10-day journey around the moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe as ~10-day mission flying around Moon (no landing) and returning to Earth splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Mr. Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen'; R3/R4: identical crew listing
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly these four as the crew.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since ... Apollo program 53 years ago' (1973, Apollo 17 1972); R2: 'last time ... Apollo 17, in December 1972'; R3: 'first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972'; R4: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed deep space flight since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test their Orion capsule ... making sure ... systems are working properly ... for future missions'; R2: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey ... for docking with lunar landers'; R3: 'testing handling ... critical for future deep space missions'; R4: 'test mission ... needed for future lunar missions'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe as test flight validating systems for future lunar missions/landings.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is currently in orbit following a successful liftoff
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II crew begins first day in space ... orbiting the Earth'; R2: 'now in a stable orbit'; R3: 'placed Orion into its high Earth orbit ... stable high Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Post-liftoff updates confirm Orion in Earth orbit performing orbital maneuvers.
